---
title: MCP Console Python
description: >-
  Python clients and framework adapters for persistent R, Python, and SQL
  sessions.
---

The `mcp_console` package gives Python applications and model frameworks a persistent R, Python, and SQL session.
A model requests a `send` tool call, Console evaluates the cell, and the framework sends the output back to the model.
Variables and loaded packages stay available for later cells in the same session.

## Install

Use Python 3.11 or newer and install the extra for your framework.
For example, to use Anthropic:

```sh
pip install 'mcp-console[anthropic]'
```

The extra installs the framework and MCP client dependencies alongside Console.
Set your provider's API key and choose a model before running a model example; each reference page lists its setup.
The examples read the model ID from `OPENAI_MODEL` or `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` so you can use a model available to your account.

## Choose an integration

Each link below includes a complete usage example and explains who owns the connection and tool loop.

| Framework        | Extra           | Use an existing Console connection                                                  | Let the framework open Console                        |
| ---------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| chatlas          | `chatlas`       | [tool()](reference/chatlas.tool.qmd)                                                | [register()](reference/chatlas.register.qmd)          |
| OpenAI Responses | `openai`        | [responses_tool()](reference/openai.responses_tool.qmd), with an explicit tool loop |                                                       |
| OpenAI Agents    | `openai-agents` | [agents_tool()](reference/openai.agents_tool.qmd)                                   | [agents_server()](reference/openai.agents_server.qmd) |
| Anthropic        | `anthropic`     | [tool()](reference/anthropic.tool.qmd)                                              | [tools()](reference/anthropic.tools.qmd)              |
| Thread SDK       | `codex`         |                                                                                     | [server()](reference/codex.server.qmd)                |

The adapters use the connected server's `send` schema.
The Responses and native MCP integrations preserve images, allowing a model to inspect a plot that Console produces.
The `chatlas.tool()`, `agents_tool()`, and `anthropic.tool()` adapters return text, representing images as MIME placeholders.

## Call Console directly

Install `mcp-console[client]` to run cells without a model or API key.
Use [MCPConsole](reference/MCPConsole.qmd) for synchronous code or [AsyncMCPConsole](reference/AsyncMCPConsole.qmd) for async code.
Keep one connection for the conversation:

```python
from mcp_console import MCPConsole

with MCPConsole() as console:
    print(console.send(python="values = [12, 15, 18, 20, 25]; values"))
    print(console.send(python="import statistics; statistics.mean(values)"))
```

The context starts the server and closes it when you leave.
Create adapters inside the context and keep it open until the model finishes using its tools.
Reconnect starts a new session; recreate adapters after reconnecting.

`timeout_ms` limits how long a call waits for output; it does not cancel execution.
If a call returns `[running; poll with an empty send]`, call `send()` without code to collect the remaining output before submitting another cell.
See [send()](reference/AsyncMCPConsole.qmd#send) for a polling example and [Requirements](reference/Requirements.qmd) for adding packages to the worker environment.

The [Python integration guide](https://t-kalinowski.github.io/mcp-console/PYTHON.html) also covers source-checkout installation and requirements inspection.
